# Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Implementation Specification > Implementation companion to `OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md`. > > Scope: define the smallest complete first build of Ocean Desktop's Dynamic > Island and its keyboard-first session focus/search mode. This is deliberately > concrete: data contracts, components, files, state transitions, keyboard > routing, CSS geometry, acceptance checks, and explicitly deferred work. > > The practical delivery sequence and commit gates live in > [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md). ## Decision summary Build this before a permanent left rail. The first release is **not** a generalized desktop task system. It is a Tauri-only, titlebar-adjacent focus surface backed by the existing daemon session catalogue. ### V1 ships - compact Dynamic Island in the desktop header - focused session identity plus a count of active-background sessions - click to open an Island overlay - overlay lists active/recent sessions with project/path/branch/origin metadata - selecting a result calls the existing `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and moves that session into the center transcript - `⌘P` opens that same overlay in search mode - fuzzy search over existing session metadata - arrow keys, Enter, Escape, click-outside behavior ### V1 does not ship - inline reply to a background session - cross-session live streaming in the Island - server-side/session-content semantic search - approvals, CI, GitHub, browser, rooms, Council, files, or PR results - a left rail - a replacement for the existing web/extension Sessions modal Those are follow-on waves after the core focus interaction is proven. ## Phase 2A — approved read-only attention slice V1 proved the focus loop. The next slice turns the expanded Island into a truthful cross-session activity surface without giving it mutation authority. This section is binding for Phase 2A. ### Authoritative sources Use the daemon's existing global snapshots: - `GET /v1/requests` for queued, running, waiting-for-permission, cancelling, and errored request state across sessions. - `GET /v1/permissions` for currently pending permissions and their request/session/tool/reason metadata. - `GET /v1/agent/sessions` remains the title/project/path lookup catalogue. Poll the two attention snapshots every three seconds while the Tauri Island is mounted, refresh immediately on mount and overlay open, and retain the last good snapshot if one request fails. This is an interim read-only projection, not a new runtime store. A unified replayable daemon attention stream remains the later target. Never infer running, blocked, failed, or complete state from session timestamps. Timestamps may order authoritative items; they may not create them. ### Projection rules Project the snapshot into these display states: - `NeedsHuman`: every pending permission; de-duplicate its matching `waiting_for_permission` request. - `Running`: queued or running requests. - `Cancelling`: cancelling requests. - `Failed`: the three newest errored requests in the current daemon registry. - Omit completed and cancelled requests. Join `session_id` to the fetched session catalogue for title/project display. Use a short session id fallback when the catalogue has not caught up. Do not render raw permission `args` in the Island; the existing transcript-adjacent permission surface remains the detail/action authority. ### Compact-state priority The closed chip preserves the focused session title. Its trailing status reads, in priority order: 1. ` need attention` 2. ` running` 3. existing ` recent` The dot uses `--warn` for human attention, the existing live accent for running, and the normal/empty treatment otherwise. No pulse or decorative animation. The accessible label and one polite live region announce the same factual count. ### Expanded interaction The popover remains one dialog and one material surface. When activity exists, render an `Activity` section between search and session results: - needs-human items first, then failed, cancelling, and running; - one plain summary row per item, with state, session title, and concise detail; - clicking or pressing Enter on a summary toggles its inline disclosure; - the disclosure may show project, tool/request state, and bounded reason; - one ghost `Open session` action focuses the associated session through `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and closes the Island. Attention controls participate in a real Tab focus trap. Arrow-key/ `aria-activedescendant` session navigation remains scoped to the search input, so using a disclosure button can never accidentally switch the selected session. Escape still closes exactly one surface and restores the invoking focus. ### Explicit Phase 2A deferrals - no approve/deny inside the Island; - no inline reply/resume or stop action; - no local dismiss/read state; - no raw permission arguments; - no browser, CI, GitHub, room, or Council cards; - no claim that the polling projection is durable attention history. Those mutations follow only after the read-only state and ordering prove useful and their daemon authorization contracts are explicit. ## Existing foundations to reuse Do not recreate these systems: | Existing implementation | Reuse in Island work | | --- | --- | | `Daemon::sessions: RwSignal>` | search corpus and list data | | `Daemon::session_id: RwSignal>` | focused-session identity | | `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` | sole session focus/switch operation | | `sessions.rs::split_origin`, `fmt_relative_time`, `session_root`, project lookup | display metadata and normalized search text | | `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` behavior | fuzzy scoring semantics; extract/move to a shared search helper rather than copy it | | `PaletteView` keyboard pattern | input autofocus, ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, backdrop click | | `app.rs` `window_event_listener(ev::keydown, ...)` | `⌘P` global shortcut and overlay Escape priority | | `host::running_in_tauri()` | mount/gating boundary | | `styles/chrome.css` titlebar model | titlebar position and drag-region rules | Important fact: today `Daemon::switch_session` replaces the active transcript and reconnects its SSE/permission streams. The Island must call it; it must not attempt a second transcript/session runtime of its own. ## User-facing model ### Terminology - **Focused session**: the daemon's current `session_id`; it owns the center transcript and composer. - **Background session**: any other persisted session in the catalogue. V1 treats "recent" as the only reliable activity signal. - **Island**: compact titlebar control plus its expanded overlay. - **Search mode**: overlay opened by `⌘P`, with input focused. - **Browse mode**: overlay opened by click, with input present but not focused or visually secondary. Do not call every session "active" in V1. The client currently observes an SSE stream only for the focused session, so it cannot truthfully determine whether other sessions are presently generating work. The component does not mount off-Tauri, so it remains visually inert on web/extension. ### Geometry tokens ```css :root { --island-max-w: 360px; --island-popover-w: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px)); --island-top: 64px; /* header bottom + seam; revise against live Tauri shot */ } ``` ### Required layering ```text workspace pane 50 web deck 60 modal sessions 100 Island scrim/popover 120 command palette 1100 ``` The Island must sit above the workspace and ordinary panels, below `⌘K` palette. At widths too narrow for a usable popover, allow the fixed overlay to span the safe viewport width; do not introduce a different mobile design in this slice. ### Initial selectors ```css .ocean-header { position: relative; } .island-host { position: absolute; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-chip { /* compact titlebar control */ } .island-scrim { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 120; } .island-popover { position: fixed; Click chip: browse overlay opens, shows focused session first. 4. Click outside: closes. 5. Press `⌘P` from composer, workspace, and header: search opens and input has focus each time. 6. Type project, branch, title, cwd, and origin queries; confirm expected result. 7. Arrow down/up/Enter switches session and overlay closes. 8. Resize Tauri to narrow and wide widths; verify usable overlay geometry. 11. # Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Build Plan

> Practical delivery sequence for implementing
> [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md).
> This document describes how to start, what to build first, commit boundaries,
> verification gates, and when to introduce richer daemon-backed attention
> state.

## Goal

Start with a thin vertical slice that proves one complete interaction:

> **Press `⌘P` → find a session → press Enter → that session takes over the
> focused transcript.**

Once that loop is reliable and feels good, mount the same machinery in the
ambient titlebar Island. Do not attempt the entire long-term Island vision in
one pass.

## Step 0 — Protect the current worktree

The current worktree already contains unrelated modifications, including:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs`
- `crates/ocean-tauri/src/lib.rs`

Before implementation:

1. Inspect the existing diffs.
2. Determine whether they belong to another active change.
3. Create a dedicated branch or worktree for the Island build if appropriate.
4. Keep the North Star and implementation documents with the Island work.
5. Do not overwrite or revert unrelated modifications.

This prevents the titlebar/session architecture work from being mixed with an
unrelated Tauri or sessions change.

## Step 1 — Build the pure session-search model

Start with code that has no DOM, CSS, or Tauri dependency.

### Files

Add:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs`
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs`

Update the crate's module declarations as required.

### Implement

- shared fuzzy scoring extracted from `palette.rs`
- `IslandMode`
- `IslandSession`
- `IslandResult`
- `derive_island_sessions(...)`
- `island_search_text(...)`
- `search_island(...)`
- title/project/path/branch/origin normalization
- deterministic result ordering

### Reuse

Use the existing sources of truth:

- `Daemon::sessions`
- `Daemon::projects`
- `Daemon::session_id`
- `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)`
- project ownership helpers from `sessions.rs`
- session-root and origin parsing from `sessions.rs`
- fuzzy-search behavior from `palette.rs`

Do not duplicate project matching, origin parsing, or fuzzy-scoring algorithms.
Extract or safely expose shared helpers.

### Truth constraint

V1 may identify sessions as:

- focused
- recent
- background

It must not claim background sessions are actively running or waiting for a
reply. The client currently has complete live runtime observation only for the
focused session.

### Unit-test exit criteria

Tests must prove:

- focused session ranks first for an empty query
- newer background sessions sort before older sessions
- title matches outrank path-only matches
- project name is searchable
- cwd path is searchable
- branch is searchable
- origin is searchable
- zero-turn sessions remain discoverable
- origin prefixes are formatted correctly
- empty query preserves derived ordering
- result ordering is deterministic

## Step 2 — Build `⌘P` as a minimal focus switcher

Before designing the ambient chip, prove the core interaction.

### Add a minimal Island overlay

The overlay must:

- open when `⌘P` is pressed in Tauri
- fetch current sessions and projects when opened
- focus and select its search input
- show filtered session results
- support ArrowUp and ArrowDown
- support Enter to select
- support Escape to close
- close when its backdrop is clicked
- call `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` for the selected session
- close after a successful switch

The existing Sessions panel already calls:

- `Daemon::fetch_sessions()`
- `Daemon::fetch_projects()`

The Island should use those same methods when Browse or Search mode opens, so it
does not operate on a stale catalogue.

### Shortcut behavior

Initial behavior:

- `⌘P` on macOS opens Search mode
- `Ctrl+P` may be supported for parity
- intercept the shortcut only on Tauri for V1
- do not intercept browser/PWA Print behavior
- the shortcut must work while focus is in the composer, transcript, workspace,
  or header

### Keyboard behavior

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘P` / `Ctrl+P` | Open Search mode and focus/select the input |
| `Escape` | Close Island and stop propagation |
| `ArrowDown` | Select next result, wrapping |
| `ArrowUp` | Select previous result, wrapping |
| `Enter` | Focus selected session and close |
| `Tab` | Use normal focus traversal in V1 |

### Exit criteria

From any focused area in Tauri:

1. Press `⌘P`.
2. Type part of a session title, project, path, branch, or origin.
3. Navigate with ArrowUp/ArrowDown.
4. Press Enter.
5. Confirm the selected transcript loads.
6. Open `⌘P` again and confirm the old session remains discoverable.
7. Confirm the browser/PWA still retains its normal Print shortcut.

This milestone is the first complete product proof.

## Step 3 — Add the compact titlebar Island

After the search/focus loop works, mount the compact Island inside
`.ocean-header` on Tauri only.

### Compact content

Initially show:

- focused session title
- project name when space permits
- number of recent background sessions
- a subtle state dot

When no session is focused, show a quiet empty state such as:

```text
Ocean · no session
```

### Interaction

- clicking the compact Island opens Browse mode
- clicking while it is open closes it
- Browse mode uses the same overlay and result pipeline as Search mode
- selecting a session switches focus and closes the overlay

### Initial visual constraints

- maximum compact width: approximately `520px` on wide desktop headers, with narrower breakpoint caps
- truncate metadata before obscuring the session title
- do not add urgency animation without truthful attention data
- do not use multiple decorative chips in V1
- do not add hover expansion yet
- do not add inline reply yet
- the Island must not carry `data-tauri-drag-region`
- the surrounding header must remain draggable

### Exit criteria

- Island is centered cleanly in the live Tauri titlebar
- it does not overlap macOS traffic lights
- it does not overlap runtime telemetry, overflow, or workspace controls
- the Island remains interactive
- surrounding titlebar space still drags the window
- narrow windows truncate gracefully
- the web and extension surfaces do not mount the Island

## Step 4 — Unify Browse and Search modes

Use one component, one overlay, and one result pipeline.

Do not build a separate Island dropdown and quick-open palette.

### Browse mode

Opened by clicking the compact Island:

- focused session first
- recent sessions next
- search input may remain visible but visually secondary
- initial list can be limited to approximately eight visible rows
- scrolling exposes additional results

### Search mode

Opened by `⌘P`:

- input receives focus immediately
- existing query is selected or cleared according to the final interaction
  decision
- fuzzy filtering begins immediately
- first result is selected
- up to approximately twenty initial search results may be rendered

### State model

```rust
pub enum IslandMode {
    Closed,
    Browse,
    Search,
}
```

`app.rs` owns `IslandMode`, because global shortcuts and Escape ordering are
application-level concerns. The `Island` component owns local query and keyboard
selection state.

## Step 5 — Polish from the real Tauri application

Do not approve the visual treatment from generic mockups.

After the feature runs:

1. Launch the real Tauri app.
2. Capture the actual native window.
3. Test both narrow and wide window sizes.
4. Tune titlebar position and control spacing.
5. Tune typography and metadata density.
6. Remove any styling that resembles a floating web modal.
7. Verify the Island reads as one Ocean object rather than an imitation of
   Apple's iPhone Dynamic Island.

### Visual principles

- use Ocean's existing depth ramp and cyan/teal cues
- compact capsule is acceptable because it represents one living titlebar object
- use one elevated popover surface
- use tonal result-row selection rather than individually elevated cards
- avoid unnecessary shadows, pills, and nested rounded containers
- preserve the titlebar's native drag behavior

## Step 6 — Observe before expanding the product

Use the session-focused V1 before adding broad integrations.

Questions to answer from actual use:

- How many sessions are useful in the Island at once?
- Is click-to-browse useful, or does `⌘P` dominate?
- Should the focused session remain visible in the compact Island?
- Do operators want explicit pins or only recent work?
- Is inline reply better than switching focus?
- Does a rail remain necessary for deep project browsing?
- Which metadata is useful versus noisy?

Do not answer these questions through speculative UI alone.

## Step 7 — Add real attention state through the daemon

The richer Island vision requires daemon-owned cross-session truth.

The current client cannot reliably know whether a background session is:

- running
- waiting for a reply
- blocked on approval
- failed
- complete

Do not infer these states from timestamps.

### Proposed follow-up daemon contract

```rust
struct WorkAttentionItem {
    id: String,
    kind: WorkKind,
    session_id: Option<String>,
    title: String,
    detail: Option<String>,
    state: WorkState,
    updated_at: String,
    priority: u8,
}

enum WorkKind {
    Session,
    Permission,
    Browser,
    Ci,
    GitHub,
    Room,
    Council,
}

enum WorkState {
    Idle,
    Running,
    NeedsHuman,
    Failed,
    Complete,
}
```

The daemon owns the source of truth. The Island reduces and renders that state.
This preserves Ocean's many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture.

### Suggested integration order

After daemon support exists:

1. permission requests
2. background session execution
3. browser-driving work
4. CI and GitHub runs
5. Council / Longhouse activity
6. calls and rooms

## Commit sequence

Keep each commit independently understandable and testable.

### Commit 1 — Search core

Changes:

- shared fuzzy scorer
- Island data types
- session derivation
- search functions
- unit tests

Verification:

- focused UI-crate tests
- existing palette fuzzy tests
- existing session grouping tests

### Commit 2 — `⌘P` focus switcher

Changes:

- Island overlay
- session/project refresh on open
- input and result list
- keyboard behavior
- session switching
- Escape/backdrop handling

Verification:

- keyboard-only focus switch works in Tauri
- browser Print remains unaffected

### Commit 3 — Compact titlebar Island

Changes:

- Tauri-only header mount
- Browse mode
- focused title/project/recent count
- `styles/island.css`
- stylesheet wiring

Verification:

- native header interaction and drag-region checks
- no web/extension visual changes

### Commit 4 — Native polish and hardening

Changes:

- screenshot-based visual refinement
- narrow/wide layout behavior
- z-index and Escape ordering
- coexistence with `⌘K`
- accessibility labels and focus states

Verification:

- manual Tauri acceptance pass
- focused Rust/WASM checks
- web and extension regression pass

## File-level plan

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | shared fuzzy matcher extracted from palette logic |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` | Island types, derivation, search, component, unit tests |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` | `IslandMode`, Tauri mount, `⌘P`, Escape priority, registry command |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs` | expose reusable metadata/project helpers where needed |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/palette.rs` | consume shared fuzzy scorer after extraction |
| `styles/island.css` | compact Island, overlay, results, responsive geometry |
| `styles/chrome.css` | titlebar positioning adjustments only if required |
| `index.html` | Island stylesheet link |
| extension build/style wiring | update only if explicit stylesheet packaging requires it |

## First coding task

Start with **Commit 1: the pure session-search core**.

It is the best entry point because it is:

- low risk
- independently testable
- free from premature visual decisions
- reusable by Browse and Search modes
- compatible with future Island entities
- unlikely to disturb the existing web/extension UX

The first implementation session should end with tested Rust helpers—not a
partially working visual overlay.

## Definition of V1 complete

V1 is complete when:

- Tauri shows a compact Island in the header
- clicking the Island opens Browse mode
- `⌘P` opens Search mode from anywhere in the app
- sessions can be searched by existing metadata
- arrow keys and Enter switch focused sessions
- Escape and click-outside close exactly one surface
- the old focused session remains discoverable after switching
- no false cross-session activity claims are shown
- web/extension behavior remains unchanged
- the result is verified using screenshots of the actual Tauri app

- use tonal result-row selection rather than individually elevated cards
- avoid unnecessary shadows, pills, and nested rounded containers
- preserve the titlebar's native drag behavior

## Step 6 — Observe before expanding the product

Use the session-focused V1 before adding broad integrations.

Questions to answer from actual use:

- How many sessions are useful in the Island at once?
- Is click-to-browse useful, or does `⌘P` dominate?
- Should the focused session remain visible in the compact Island?
- Do operators want explicit pins or only recent work?
- Is inline reply better than switching focus?
- Does a rail remain necessary for deep project browsing?
- Which metadata is useful versus noisy?

Do not answer these questions through speculative UI alone.

## Step 7 — Add real attention state through the daemon

The richer Island vision requires daemon-owned cross-session truth.

The current client cannot reliably know whether a background session is:

- running
- waiting for a reply
- blocked on approval
- failed
- complete

Do not infer these states from timestamps.

### Proposed follow-up daemon contract

```rust
struct WorkAttentionItem {
    id: String,
    kind: WorkKind,
    session_id: Option<String>,
    title: String,
    detail: Option<String>,
    state: WorkState,
    updated_at: String,
    priority: u8,
}

enum WorkKind {
    Session,
    Permission,
    Browser,
    Ci,
    GitHub,
    Room,
    Council,
}

enum WorkState {
    Idle,
    Running,
    NeedsHuman,
    Failed,
    Complete,
}
```

The daemon owns the source of truth. The Island reduces and renders that state.
This preserves Ocean's many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture.

### Suggested integration order

After daemon support exists:

1. permission requests
2. background session execution
3. browser-driving work
4. CI and GitHub runs
5. Council / Longhouse activity
6. calls and rooms

## Commit sequence

Keep each commit independently understandable and testable.

### Commit 1 — Search core

Changes:

- shared fuzzy scorer
- Island data types
- session derivation
- search functions
- unit tests

Verification:

- focused UI-crate tests
- existing palette fuzzy tests
- existing session grouping tests

### Commit 2 — `⌘P` focus switcher

Changes:

- Island overlay
- session/project refresh on open
- input and result list
- keyboard behavior
- session switching
- Escape/backdrop handling

Verification:

- keyboard-only focus switch works in Tauri
- browser Print remains unaffected

### Commit 3 — Compact titlebar Island

Changes:

- Tauri-only header mount
- Browse mode
- focused title/project/recent count
- `styles/island.css`
- stylesheet wiring

Verification:

- native header interaction and drag-region checks
- no web/extension visual changes

### Commit 4 — Native polish and hardening

Changes:

- screenshot-based visual refinement
- narrow/wide layout behavior
- z-index and Escape ordering
- coexistence with `⌘K`
- accessibility labels and focus states

Verification:

- manual Tauri acceptance pass
- focused Rust/WASM checks
- web and extension regression pass

## File-level plan

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | shared fuzzy matcher extracted from palette logic |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` | Island types, derivation, search, component, unit tests |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` | `IslandMode`, Tauri mount, `⌘P`, Escape priority, registry command |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs` | expose reusable metadata/project helpers where needed |

| `styles/island.css` | compact Island, overlay, results, responsive geometry |
| `styles/chrome.css` | titlebar positioning adjustments only if required |
| `index.html` | Island stylesheet link |
| extension build/style wiring | update only if explicit stylesheet packaging requires it |

## First coding task

Start with **Commit 1: the pure session-search core**.

It is the best entry point because it is:

- low risk
- independently testable
- free from premature visual decisions
- reusable by Browse and Search modes
- compatible with future Island entities
- unlikely to disturb the existing web/extension UX

The first implementation session should end with tested Rust helpers—not a
partially working visual overlay.

## Definition of V1 complete

V1 is complete when:

- Tauri shows a compact Island in the header
- clicking the Island opens Browse mode
- `⌘P` opens Search mode from anywhere in the app
- sessions can be searched by existing metadata
- arrow keys and Enter switch focused sessions
- Escape and click-outside close exactly one surface
- the old focused session remains discoverable after switching
- no false cross-session activity claims are shown
- web/extension behavior remains unchanged
- the result is verified using screenshots of the actual Tauri app

## Review

- **High — Activity rows can retain stale state and details across polls.** `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs:856-873` keys `<For>` rows only by `item.id`, then captures `item_class`, `state_label`, `session_title`, `summary_detail`, and detail fields as non-reactive values. Leptos keyed iteration retains an existing row when its key is unchanged; it does not rerun the child closure for updated data. A request therefore can remain visibly `Running` after the same request ID changes to `Cancelling` or `Errored`, and updated messages/session metadata can remain stale. This breaks the Phase 2A requirement that the polling view truthfully project authoritative state (`docs/OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md:69-78,100-108`). The chip counts are separately reactive, so the chip can say attention is needed while the corresponding retained card still says Running.

- **Medium — The composer IME guard does not cover slash-menu keyboard handling.** In `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs:1464-1534`, slash-menu ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Enter/Tab handling executes before any `is_composing()` check. The new guard is only applied to ordinary Enter submission at `app.rs:1535-1543`. If composition text begins with `/` and matches a slash command, Enter used to accept an IME candidate can execute the selected command and clear the input (`app.rs:1493-1518`); composition arrow keys are also intercepted. The composition guard needs to precede the slash-menu key switch (while preserving the intended non-composing behavior).

### Verified correct

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/daemon.rs:767-817,2625-2647` matches the current daemon wire types for `GET /v1/requests` and `GET /v1/permissions`, ignores raw permission `args`, and only replaces each signal after a decoded `ok: true` response.
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs:455-463,476-480,531-543` implements the specified 3-second mounted polling plus immediate mount/open refresh. The current in-flight guard at `daemon.rs:2602-2610` prevents overlapping polls.
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs:190-203,226-232` implements the required projection and ordering: pending permission de-duplication, queued/running, cancelling, newest three errors, and omission of completed/cancelled requests.
- The Phase 2A UI remains read-only apart from the approved focus action: the only card action is `Open session` via `Daemon::switch_session` at `island.rs:939-960`; no approve, deny, reply, resume, or stop endpoint is called.
- Explicit EventSource retirement closes both focused-session transports before reconnecting (`daemon.rs:1775-1785`) and stores/retire-closes the newly opened agent and permission sources (`daemon.rs:1864-1870,2023-2029`). No concrete cancellation race was found in inspection.
- The dialog traps Tab among the input, disclosure summaries, and enabled Open buttons (`island.rs:597-641`), scopes Arrow/Enter session navigation to the search input (`island.rs:644-695`), and stops composing/Escape handling appropriately inside the Island (`island.rs:586-595`).

### Validation notes

- Native Rust tests pass, but the WASM check could not run because `wasm32-unknown-unknown` is not installed. Consequently, the new `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` EventSource handle code and browser DOM behavior were not compiler/runtime validated in this environment.
- The requested repository-root `plan.md` and `progress.md` do not exist. Review used `docs/OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md` and `docs/OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` instead.
- No project/source files were modified by this review.
